data.long_meaning: Eesaa is the Arabic name for Jesus, son of Mary, a prophet in Islam. He is considered one of the most important prophets in the Quran. The name Eesaa carries the meaning “Jesus, son of Mary” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Eesaa usually hope their child will grow to embody jesus, son of mary and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_urdu.name: عیسی
in_urdu.meaning: رسول، نبی، حضرت عیسی عليه السلام کا نام

in_hindi.name: ईसा
in_hindi.long_meaning: ईसा एक पवित्र नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है मसीहा, नबी या पैगंबर। यह नाम हज़रत ईसा सल्लल्लाहु अलैहि वसल्लम के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है, जो इस्लामी परंपरा में एक महत्वपूर्ण नबी माने जाते हैं।

in_pashto.name: عيسى

data.cultural_impact: Eesaa's name holds a significant place in Islamic and Middle Eastern culture, as he is widely recognized and revered in Islam as a prophet and messenger of Allah. The prophecy of Jesus' arrival was mentioned in the Old Testament and the Torah, and his birth, life, death, and resurrection are detailed in the New Testament in Christianity. In the Islamic culture, Eesaa is often depicted as a powerful and merciful figure, who was born from the Virgin Mary without a father, a miracle that underscores the belief in divine intervention in human affairs.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic theology, Eesaa is considered to be a beloved prophet of Allah, sent to guide the Children of Israel and to validate the truth of previous prophets, including Moses and Muhammad. He is believed to have been born as a sign of Allah's mercy to humanity, and his life and teachings serve as an example of true devotion to God. Muslims believe that Eesaa, like all prophets, was always obedient to Allah and that his mission was guided by divine inspiration. The spiritual significance of his name is emphasized through the Quranic verses that extoll Eesaa's virtues and prophesy his role in salvation. (Maryam 19:21-35, 3:45-50)
